gate: M10/1 Active; transport/seek foundation verified, app integration remains open
deliverable: MapGyver now owns reusable per-media transport policy on Golden Time; Golden Video can seek in exact original stream timestamps across EOF without retaining old codec output. No Video media/Parameter/preview wiring or complete codec-gate acceptance is claimed.

transport.owner: apps/mapgyver/src/media/video; one non-Clone MediaTransport owner, immutable TransportSample observations for future channel/Reference consumers
transport.behavior: Paused-at-zero/rate1/loop-off defaults; play/pause/stop/seek; continuous positive/zero/reverse rational rates; non-looping endpoint hold/restart; loop cycles and explicit-control epochs; longest-file timeline and shorter-channel hold; exact supplied decoder timestamp steps pause playback; duration-change and clock/overflow validation.
transport.clock: Golden Time maps from one monotonic anchor. Readers and repeated consumer samples do not advance or accumulate rounded frame periods. Explicit controls change epochs; loop cycles distinguish equal wrapped positions from different source lifetimes.
transport.limits: The selected-channel neighbour resolver and actual shared Reference wiring are not implemented by these pure policy tests. Runtime fields are not persisted authored settings; the pending typed Parameter adapter must supply configuration and all public callers.

decode_seek.api: SoftwareDecoder::seek_before(original_stream_timestamp); direct public FFmpeg av_seek_frame binding with the validated selected-stream index and backward-keyframe policy
decode_seek.ownership: Keep one file/demux owner; prepare a fresh bounded codec context per discontinuity and explicitly set packet time base. Codec thread count and image admission limits are retained. Previously returned frames retain independent reference-counted storage. Failed seeks poison the decoder; out-of-declared-range control validation preserves its current state.
decode_seek.proof: All three real common-codec fixtures seek to presentation indices5,0,4,2,1 after a full linear drain. Each decodes forward to the exact original timestamp and independently checks its encoded luma level, rejecting stale frames. Clean EOF rewinds; poisoned decoders cannot hide errors by seeking.

software.initial_filtered_check: Eight earlier transport cases pass under --no-default-features; the complete default-feature suite additionally covers the later duration/cycle-overflow case. Existing sender-catalog dead-code warnings under no-default-features are retained; this configuration is not claimed strict-clean.
software.protocol_ui: No wire DTO, authored settings or UI source changed. Current generated-contract regressions run in the full app suite; no hand-maintained TypeScript declaration is added.

corrected_failure: The first seek implementation using global microseconds plus codec flush failed on HEVC. A direct original-stream seek with the same flush also failed: after seeking from index4 back to index2, receive_frame returned the old PTS5005 frame before any newly read packet. Replacing codec-owned reorder/drain state and setting the packet time base resolves the retained regression across all three codecs. This is evidence from the pinned binding/build fixture, not a general claim about every FFmpeg decoder or upstream version.
remaining: Expose Video through typed media/File/transport Parameters and the generic Inspector; complete commands/functions/callbacks/snippets/history/project parity, selected-channel frame-step resolution and shared Reference integration. Add bounded/coalesced decode workers, upload/hardware-frame paths, file/device recovery, HAP and full first-pass packaging/performance. Seek codec-initialization cost must be measured in M10/4; these software fixtures do not prove actual-app playback, GPU residency or sustained cadence.
